stem:
A 48-year-old man presents with recurrent duodenal ulcers refractory to proton-pump inhibitor therapy. He reports daily watery diarrhea and epigastric pain. Fasting serum gastrin is markedly elevated, and secretin administration fails to suppress gastrin levels. Abdominal imaging shows a 2-cm mass in the wall of the duodenum.

Which of the following mechanisms best explains his hypersecretory gastric acid state?

options.label: A
options.text: Excess hormone from the tumor directly stimulates parietal cells to secrete hydrochloric acid
options.misconception: None; autonomous gastrin drives parietal-cell acid secretion.
options.explanation: Gastrin is the principal stimulatory hormone for parietal cells; a gastrin-secreting tumor causes excess HCl production, recurrent ulcers, and often diarrhea.

options.label: B
options.text: Chief-cell hyperplasia alone increases acid without parietal-cell stimulation
options.misconception: The enzyme-secreting cell is being cast as the acid source.
options.explanation: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen, not acid; hyperacidity in gastrinoma reflects gastrin-driven parietal-cell stimulation.

options.label: C
options.text: Antral G cells secrete excess gastrin that is blocked from reaching parietal cells
options.misconception: Antral mucus cells are being mistaken for acid-secreting cells.
options.explanation: Antral cells secrete mucus and gastrin; they do not produce hydrochloric acid, which comes from parietal cells in the gastric body.

options.label: D
options.text: Pancreatic duct cells secrete acid to compensate for bicarbonate loss
options.misconception: A bicarbonate-secreting cell is being inverted to an acid source.
options.explanation: Pancreatic duct cells secrete bicarbonate-rich fluid to neutralize gastric acid in the duodenum; they do not cause gastric hypersecretion.

options.label: E
options.text: Jejunal enterocytes absorb acid, lowering luminal pH in the stomach
options.misconception: Absorptive cells are being treated as gastric acid secretors.
options.explanation: Enterocytes absorb nutrients in the jejunum; gastric acid hypersecretion in this syndrome reflects autonomous gastrin stimulation of parietal cells.

context: Learning objective: link gastrinoma to parietal-cell hypersecretion. Gastrin stimulates parietal cells to produce HCl; excess gastrin causes refractory PUD and diarrhea (Zollinger-Ellison syndrome).
